## Load Necessary Libraries

```{r lib_load}
library(tidyverse)   # data wrangling & ggplot2
library(janitor)     # functions for examining and cleaning dirty data
library(here)        # Find files within a project
library(car)         # vif()
library(lmtest)      # Breusch–Pagan test
library(ggpubr)      # Automatically print the regression equation for ggplot
library(spgwr)       # Functions for computing geographically weighted regressions
library(tidymodels)  # collection of packages for modeling and machine learning
library(finetune)    # enhances the 'tune' package by providing more specialized methods
library(xgboost)     # Extreme Gradient Boosting
library(bundle)      # Serialize Model Objects with a Consistent Interface
library(psych)       # group statistics, including correlations and factor analysis
library(kableExtra)  # let R Markdown generate a LaTeX‐based PDF

library(olsrr)       # package for p-value backward elimination
```

## Importing and Organizing Data

```{r data_import}
df <- read_csv(here("data", "salesSFapr2023toMarch2025Updated.csv")) |>
  rename_with(toupper)    # clean_names()
```

## Organize Data I

```{r data_org_1}
# ─── 1. Price Categories ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df <- df |> 
  mutate(   
    PRICECLASS = case_when(    # Lines 25 -> 34
      SALEPRICE < 48000                        ~ 1,
      SALEPRICE < 67000  & SALEPRICE >= 48000  ~ 2,
      SALEPRICE < 94000  & SALEPRICE >= 67000  ~ 3,
      SALEPRICE < 134000 & SALEPRICE >= 94000  ~ 4,
      SALEPRICE >= 134000                      ~ 5
    ),
    PRICECLASS = factor(       # Lines 36 -> 41
      PRICECLASS,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "Below 48000", "48000 to 67000", "67000 to 94000", "94000 to 134000", "134000+"
      )
    )
  )

df <- df |>  
  # ─── 2. Filter to Relevant Styles    Lines 60 -> 67
  dplyr::filter(SRESB_STYLE %in% c("SINGLE FAMILY", "1/2 DUPLEX", "ROW HOUSE")) |> 
  # ─── 3. Deduplicate Records    Lines 93 -> 122
  arrange(PARCELNO, SALEPRICE, SALEDATE) |>
  group_by(PARCELNO, SALEPRICE, SALEDATE) |>
  mutate(PRIMARYFIRST = row_number() == 1, PRIMARYLAST = row_number() == n()) |>
  ungroup() |> dplyr::filter(PRIMARYLAST) |> 
  # ─── 4. Exclude Assessment‐Equal Sales    Lines 129 -> 140
  mutate(
    PRICEISASMT_RATIO  = AVWHENSOLD / SALEPRICE,
    PRICEISASMT_RATIO2 = if_else(between(PRICEISASMT_RATIO, .90, 1.10), 1, PRICEISASMT_RATIO),
    PRICEISASMT        = if_else(PRICEISASMT_RATIO == 1, 0L, 1L)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(PRICEISASMT == 1) |> 
  # ─── 5. Outlier Removal    Lines 71 -> 87
  mutate(
    OUT = case_when(
      STOTALSQFT      < 400   ~ 1L,
      SRESB_FLOORAREA < 400   ~ 1L,
      SALEPRICE       < 10000 ~ 1L,
      TRUE                    ~ 0L
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(OUT == 0) |> 
  # ─── 6. Story‐Style Dummies    9. Year‐Built Era  Lines 225 -> 330    
  mutate(
    ONESTORY            = as.integer(SRESB_STYHGT <= 2),
    TWOSTORY            = as.integer(SRESB_STYHGT > 2 & SRESB_STYHGT <= 5),
    SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY = as.integer(SRESB_STYLE == "SINGLE FAMILY" & ONESTORY == 1),
    SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY = as.integer(SRESB_STYLE == "SINGLE FAMILY" & TWOSTORY == 1),
    HALF_DUPLEX1STORY   = as.integer(SRESB_STYLE == "1/2 DUPLEX" & ONESTORY == 1),
    HALF_DUPLEX2STORY   = as.integer(SRESB_STYLE == "1/2 DUPLEX" & TWOSTORY == 1),
    ERABUILT = case_when(
      SRESB_YEARBUILT <  1910                           ~ 1,
      SRESB_YEARBUILT <  1930 & SRESB_YEARBUILT >= 1910 ~ 2,
      SRESB_YEARBUILT <  1946 & SRESB_YEARBUILT >= 1930 ~ 3,
      SRESB_YEARBUILT <  1961 & SRESB_YEARBUILT >= 1946 ~ 4,
      SRESB_YEARBUILT <= 1990 & SRESB_YEARBUILT >= 1961 ~ 5,
      SRESB_YEARBUILT >  1990                           ~ 6
    ),
    YB_PRE_1929     = as.integer(ERABUILT %in% c(1,2)), YB_1930_TO_1945 = as.integer(ERABUILT == 3),
    YB_1946_TO_1960 = as.integer(ERABUILT == 4), YB_POST_1961 = as.integer(ERABUILT %in% c(5,6))
  ) |> 
  # ─── 7. Condition Dummies    Lines 334 -> 386
  mutate(
    EXCELLENT = as.integer(SCOND == 0), VERY_GOOD = as.integer(SCOND == 1),
    GOOD      = as.integer(SCOND == 2), AVERAGE   = as.integer(SCOND == 3),
    FAIR      = as.integer(SCOND == 4), POOR      = as.integer(SCOND == 5),
    VERY_POOR_UNSOUND  = as.integer(SCOND %in% c(6,7)),
    TWO_PLUS_BATHS = as.integer(SRESB_FULLBATHS >= 2), TWO_BATHS = as.integer(SRESB_FULLBATHS == 2),
    POWDER_ROOM    = as.integer(SRESB_HALFBATHS >= 1), ONE_BATH  = as.integer(SRESB_FULLBATHS == 1),
    TOTAL_BATHS    = as.integer(SRESB_FULLBATHS + 0.5 * SRESB_HALFBATHS),
    FIREPLACE      = as.integer(SRESB_FIREPLACE >= 1)
  ) |> 
  # ─── 8. Basement & Garage    Lines 393 -> 473
  mutate(
    PCTCRAWL       = SRESB_CRAWSPACE / SRESB_GROUNDAREA,
    PCTSLAB        = SRESB_SLABAREA / SRESB_GROUNDAREA,
    PCTBSMNT       = SRESB_BASEMENTAREA / SRESB_GROUNDAREA,
    CRAWL          = as.integer(PCTCRAWL > PCTBSMNT & PCTCRAWL > PCTSLAB),
    SLAB           = as.integer(PCTSLAB  > PCTCRAWL & PCTSLAB  > PCTBSMNT),
    GARAGE         = as.integer(SRESB_GARAGEAREA >= 200),
    ONE_CAR_GARAGE = as.integer(SREB_GARTYPE == 1),
    TWO_CAR_GARAGE = as.integer(SREB_GARTYPE == 2),
    GARAGESPACES   = case_when(
      SRESB_GARAGEAREA > 200 & SRESB_GARAGEAREA < 420 ~ 1,
      SRESB_GARAGEAREA > 419 & SRESB_GARAGEAREA < 600 ~ 2,
      SRESB_GARAGEAREA > 599 & SRESB_GARAGEAREA < 820 ~ 3, SRESB_GARAGEAREA > 819 ~ 4
    ),
    LN_GARAGESPACES = log(GARAGESPACES)
  ) |> 
  # ─── 9. Quality & Street Class    Lines 478 -> 544
  mutate(
    QABOVE_AVG      = as.integer(SRESB_BLDGCLASS %in% c(3,4,5)),
    Q_AVG           = as.integer(SRESB_BLDGCLASS == 2),
    QBELOW_AVG      = as.integer(SRESB_BLDGCLASS %in% c(0,1)),
    ARTERIAL        = as.integer(RD_CLASS == "A31"),
    FORCED_AIR      = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT %in% c(0,1)),
    HOT_WATER       = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 2), ELEC_BASEBOARD = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 3),
    ELEC_RADIANT = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 4), RADIANT_FLOOR  = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 5),
    ELEC_WALL       = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 6), SPACE_HEATER   = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 7),
    WALL            = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 8), CENTRAL_AIR    = as.integer(SRESB_HEAT == 9),
    SIZE = case_when(
      SRESB_FLOORAREA <   830                            ~ 1,
      SRESB_FLOORAREA <   1018 & SRESB_FLOORAREA >= 830  ~ 2,
      SRESB_FLOORAREA <   1266 & SRESB_FLOORAREA >= 1018 ~ 3,
      SRESB_FLOORAREA <   1659 & SRESB_FLOORAREA >= 1266 ~ 4,
      SRESB_FLOORAREA >=  1659                           ~ 5
    ),
    SMALLEST = as.integer(SIZE == 1), SMALL = as.integer(SIZE == 2),
    AVG = as.integer(SIZE == 3),      LARGE = as.integer(SIZE == 4),
    LARGEST = as.integer(SIZE == 5)
  ) |> 
  # ─── 10. Building Size & Lot Ratios    Lines 551 -> 593
  mutate(
    RATIO                  = SESTTCV / SALEPRICE,
    SPPSF                  = SALEPRICE / SRESB_FLOORAREA,
    BASE_BLDGSIZE          = case_when(
                             SRESB_STYLE == "SINGLE FAMILY" ~ 1056,
                             SRESB_STYLE == "1/2 DUPLEX"    ~ 840,
                             TRUE                           ~ NA_real_
                           ),
    BASE_BLDGSIZE_RATIO    = SRESB_FLOORAREA / BASE_BLDGSIZE,
    LN_BASE_BLDGSIZE_RATIO = log(BASE_BLDGSIZE_RATIO),
    LANDRATIO              = STOTALSQFT / case_when(
                             SRESB_STYLE == "SINGLE FAMILY" ~ 4599,
                             SRESB_STYLE == "1/2 DUPLEX"    ~ 3180,
                             TRUE                           ~ NA_real_
                           ),
    LANDRATIO2             = pmin(LANDRATIO, if_else(SRESB_STYLE == "SINGLE FAMILY",4,3)),
    LN_LANDRATIO           = log(LANDRATIO2),
    SALEDATE      = as_date(SALEDATE),
    MONTHS        = interval(min(SALEDATE), SALEDATE) %/% months(1), # LINE 498
    MONTHS_1TO9   = case_when(MONTHS <= 9  ~ MONTHS, TRUE ~ 9),
    MONTHS_10TO16 = case_when(MONTHS <= 9  ~ 0, MONTHS <= 16 ~ MONTHS - 9, TRUE ~ 7),
    MONTHS_17TO24 = case_when(MONTHS <= 16 ~ 0, TRUE ~ MONTHS - 16),
    LN_SPPSF      = log(SPPSF),
    LN_PRICE      = log(SALEPRICE),
    LNSBLDSF      = log(SRESB_FLOORAREA), SBLDSFINT = SRESB_FLOORAREA - 432,
    # LNSBLDSFINT   = log(SBLDSFINT),  # LINEs 650 -> 658
  )
```

## Organize Data II

```{r data_org_2}
RATE1 <- 0.004818; RATE2 <- 0.016146; RATE3 <- 0.0; END_INDEX <- 1.17

df <- df |> 
  # ─── 11. Time Variables & Price Adjustment    Lines 520 -> 532
  mutate(
    PRICE_INDEX = (1 + RATE1)^MONTHS_1TO9 * (1 + RATE2)^MONTHS_10TO16 * (1 + RATE3)^MONTHS_17TO24,
    TAF         = END_INDEX / PRICE_INDEX,
    TASP        = SALEPRICE * TAF,
    LN_TASP     = log(TASP),
    TASPPSF     = TASP / SRESB_FLOORAREA
  )
psych::describe(df$PRICE_INDEX)
# graphing(df, MONTHS, PRICE_INDEX, 'cyan', 'Months', 'Price Index', 'Index By Month')
  
```

## Create Models

```{r mod_make_1}
# Initial full model ***
full_model_1 <- lm(LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL + CRAWL + SLAB + SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY +
                   HALF_DUPLEX1STORY + HALF_DUPLEX2STORY + SMALLEST + SMALL + LARGE + LARGEST +
                   AVG + TWO_PLUS_BATHS + POWDER_ROOM + LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE +
                   EXCELLENT + VERY_GOOD + GOOD + AVERAGE + FAIR + POOR + VERY_POOR_UNSOUND +
                   QABOVE_AVG + QBELOW_AVG + Q_AVG +
                   YB_PRE_1929 + YB_1930_TO_1945 + YB_1946_TO_1960 + YB_POST_1961 +
                   HOT_WATER + ELEC_BASEBOARD + ELEC_WALL + WALL + CENTRAL_AIR + ELEC_RADIANT +
                   RADIANT_FLOOR + SPACE_HEATER + MONTHS_1TO9 + MONTHS_10TO16 + MONTHS_17TO24,
                 data = df, na.action = na.omit)

# Perform backward stepwise regression
backward_model_1 <- stats::step(full_model_1, direction = "backward")

summary(backward_model_1)    # View the summary of the final model
```

```{r mod_1_stats}
# The tidy() function from the broom package converts the model output
# into a clean data frame with one row for each coefficient.
model_1_summary <- tidy(backward_model_1)

model_1_summary |>
  # We don't usually plot the p-value for the intercept
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = p.value, y = reorder(term, p.value))) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  # Add a vertical line for the common significance threshold (alpha = 0.05)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  # Using a log scale for the x-axis is often essential for p-values,
  # as they can be clustered near zero.
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "P-Values for Predictors in Model I",
    subtitle = "Predicting log SPPSF",
    x = "P-Value (log scale)",
    y = "Predictor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Entire XGBoost Pipeline

```{r splitfeats}
# 1. Initial Data Split
# We'll split the data into a training set and a testing set.
# The training set is used for model development and tuning.
# The testing set is held out until the very end to provide an unbiased
# estimate of the final model's performance.
set.seed(123) # for reproducibility
df_split <- initial_split(df, prop = 0.80, strata = LN_SPPSF)
df_train <- training(df_split)
df_test  <- testing(df_split)

# 2. Feature Engineering and Preprocessing with Recipes
# A 'recipe' is a series of steps for data preprocessing. This is one of the
# most powerful features of tidymodels. We will perform the following steps: 
# - Convert some integer variables that are actually categorical to factors.
# - Impute missing values.
# - Create dummy variables for categorical predictors.
# - Remove variables with zero variance (no information).
# - Normalize numeric predictors.

df_recipe <- recipe(LN_SPPSF ~ ARTERIAL + CRAWL + SLAB + LN_LANDRATIO + # LN_BASE_BLDGSIZE_RATIO +
                   SINGLE_FAMILY1STORY + SINGLE_FAMILY2STORY + HALF_DUPLEX1STORY + HALF_DUPLEX2STORY +
                   SMALLEST + SMALL + LARGE + LARGEST + AVG +
                   TWO_PLUS_BATHS + POWDER_ROOM + LN_GARAGESPACES + FIREPLACE +
                   EXCELLENT + VERY_GOOD + GOOD + AVERAGE + FAIR + POOR + VERY_POOR_UNSOUND +
                   QABOVE_AVG + QBELOW_AVG + Q_AVG +
                   YB_PRE_1929 + YB_1930_TO_1945 + YB_1946_TO_1960 + YB_POST_1961 +
                   HOT_WATER + ELEC_BASEBOARD + ELEC_WALL + WALL + CENTRAL_AIR + ELEC_RADIANT +
                   RADIANT_FLOOR + SPACE_HEATER +
                   MONTHS_1TO9 + MONTHS_10TO16 + MONTHS_17TO24, data = df_train) %>%
  # Impute missing numeric data with the median
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  # Impute missing categorical data with the most frequent value
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  # Combine infrequent categorical levels into an "other" category. This helps
  # prevent issues with rare levels that might appear in one data split but not another.
  step_other(all_nominal_predictors(), threshold = 0.01) %>%
  # step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  # Create dummy variables for all categorical predictors
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% # , one_hot = TRUE
  # Remove predictors with no variance
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  # Normalize (center and scale) all numeric predictors
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_naomit(all_predictors(), all_outcomes())  # hard drop any remaining NA

# You can "prep" and "bake" the recipe to see the results of the preprocessing
# This is an optional step for verification
prepped_recipe <- prep(df_recipe, training = df_train)
baked_data     <- bake(prepped_recipe, new_data = df_train)
glimpse(baked_data)
```

```{r save_datas, eval = FALSE}
# The save function is included in base R
save(df, df_train, df_test, file = here("data", "cod_23_25_lnsppsf_data.RData"))
```

```{r load_datas, eval = FALSE}
load('../data/cod_23_25_lnprice_data.RData')
```

```{r modspecs}
# 3. Model Specification
# We'll use an XGBoost model, which is a powerful and popular algorithm for
# tabular data and often performs very well in these types of regression tasks.
# We will tune its hyperparameters.

xgb_spec <- boost_tree(
  trees          = tune(),    # 1000
  tree_depth     = tune(),
  min_n          = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  sample_size    = tune(),
  mtry           = tune(),
  learn_rate     = tune()
) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

# 4. Create a Workflow
# A workflow bundles the recipe and the model specification together.
# This makes it much easier to manage the modeling process.

xgb_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(df_recipe) %>%
  add_model(xgb_spec)

pset <- tune::extract_parameter_set_dials(xgb_workflow)

prepped <- prep(df_recipe, training = df_train)
x       <- juice(prepped) |> dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of('LN_SPPSF'))

params  <- dials::finalize(pset, x)  # uses juiced predictors to set ranges like mtry

# 5. Hyperparameter Tuning
# We need to find the best combination of hyperparameters for our XGBoost model.
# We'll use cross-validation and a space-filling design to search the parameter space.
# Create cross-validation folds from the training data
set.seed(234)
df_folds <- vfold_cv(df_train, v = 5)
# params   <- parameters(pset) %>% finalize(juice(prepped_recipe))

# Define the grid of hyperparameters to search
# We'll use a space-filling design to explore the parameter space efficiently.
set.seed(345)
xgb_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  trees(c(300, 3000)),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  loss_reduction(),
  sample_size = sample_prop(),
  finalize(mtry(), df_train),
  learn_rate(),
  size = 30 # Number of hyperparameter combinations to try
)

# --- space-filling initial grid (replaces grid_max_entropy) ---
init_grid <- grid_space_filling(params, size = 40)

# Start the tuning process
# We'll use tune_grid() to apply our workflow to the cross-validation folds
# and test all the hyperparameter combinations.
# The `control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)` option saves the predictions for later inspection.
doParallel::registerDoParallel() # Use parallel processing to speed things up

set.seed(456)
xgb_tune_res <- tune_grid(
  xgb_workflow,
  resamples = df_folds,
  grid      = xgb_grid,
  metrics   = metric_set(rmse, rsq),
  control   = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE) # verbose = TRUE
)
```

```{r bayes, eval = FALSE}
# ... then seed Bayesian optimization with those results
bayes_res <- tune_bayes(
  xgb_workflow,
  resamples = df_folds,
  initial   = xgb_tune_res,        # or just `initial = 20` for 20 random starts
  iter      = 30,
  metrics   = metric_set(rmse, rsq),
  control   = control_bayes(verbose = TRUE)
)

best <- select_best(bayes_res, "rmse")
final_wf <- finalize_workflow(xgb_workflow, best) %>% fit(df_train)

preds <- predict(final_wf, df_test) %>% bind_cols(df_test)
rmse(preds, truth = LN_PRICE, estimate = .pred)
rsq(preds,  truth = LN_PRICE, estimate = .pred)
```


```{r makedamod}
# 8. Analyze Tuning Results and Finalize the Model
# Let's see which hyperparameters performed the best.

# Show the best performing models based on root mean squared error (RMSE)
show_best(xgb_tune_res, metric = "rmse")

# We can also visualize the results
autoplot(xgb_tune_res)

# Select the best set of hyperparameters
best_xgb_params <- select_best(xgb_tune_res, metric = "rmse")

# Finalize the workflow by updating it with the best hyperparameters
final_xgb_workflow <- finalize_workflow(
  xgb_workflow,
  best_xgb_params
)

# 9. Train the Final Model and Evaluate on the Test Set
# Now, we'll train our final model on the *entire training set* and then
# evaluate its performance on the *held-out test set*. This gives us an
# unbiased
# assessment of how our model is likely to perform on new, unseen data.
# The `last_fit()` function does this for us: it fits the final model on the
# full training set and evaluates it on the test set.
final_fit <- last_fit(final_xgb_workflow, df_split)

# Collect the metrics from the test set evaluation
test_set_metrics <- collect_metrics(final_fit)
print(test_set_metrics)

# Collect the predictions on the test set
test_set_predictions <- collect_predictions(final_fit)
print(test_set_predictions)

# Since we predicted the log10 of the price, let's transform it back
# to the original scale for interpretation.
test_set_predictions <- test_set_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    LN_SPPSF = 10^LN_SPPSF,
    .pred = 10^.pred
  )

# Visualize the final predictions vs actual values
ggplot(test_set_predictions, aes(x = LN_SPPSF, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(color = "red", lty = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs. Predicted Sale Prices on the Test Set",
    x = "Actual Sale Price",
    y = "Predicted Sale Price"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  coord_obs_pred() +
  theme_minimal()

# You can now use the `final_fit` object to make predictions on new data.
# The workflow is stored inside:
final_model_object <- extract_workflow(final_fit)
```

## Custom Functions

```{r functions}
ftable <- function(data, variable, digits = 1) {
# data : data frame | variable : unquoted column name | digits : num decimals for the percent
  tbl <- data |>                               # 1) build the basic tabyl, add % formatting and totals
    tabyl({{ variable }}) |>                   # frequency table
    adorn_pct_formatting(digits = digits) |>   # "12.3%"
    adorn_totals()                              # add a "Total" column
  mat <- t(tbl)                                 # 2) transpose to get categories across the top
  colnames(mat) <- rep("", ncol(mat))           # 3) blank out the auto-generated 1,2,3… column names
  print(mat)                                    # return as a matrix, or wrap in kable() downstream
}

graphing <- function(data, x, y, color, xlab, ylab, title) {
  xq <- enquo(x)
  yq <- enquo(y)
  ggplot(data, aes(x = !!xq, y = !!yq)) +
    geom_point() +
    stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = color) +
    stat_regline_equation(
      aes(label =  paste(after_stat(eq.label), after_stat(adj.rr.label), sep = "~~~")),
      label.x.npc = 0.2,    # use "npc" coordinates 0–1 in panel
      label.y.npc = 0.8
    ) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```
